summary: The existing abstractions cover vector retrieval and federation, but not LanceDB’s FTS/hybrid capabilities, fused-score provenance, or process-concurrent persistence. The design should make those contracts explicit before implementation and validate them with restart, filtering, freshness, offline, and multiprocessing tests.

suggestions.title: Define an explicit LanceDB capability contract
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractStore` requires vector search but has no FTS or hybrid method, while `SearchOrigin` exposes only `search` and `fts_search`. Add precise LanceDB-specific `fulltext_search` and `hybrid_search` contracts, with the origin selecting a mode instead of relying on undocumented kwargs or a generic future hybrid API.

suggestions.title: Preserve hybrid component scores and conventions
suggestions.rationale: `SearchResult` and `OriginHit` currently carry only one score plus native rank. A fused LanceDB result needs its fusion score, vector/lexical component scores or ranks, and direction/convention; otherwise native RRF relevance is lost or confused with vector distance. Add a typed backwards-compatible payload or reserved provenance fields, and keep the toolkit’s BM25 merge score separate.

suggestions.title: Specify one filter and parent-visibility policy for every Lance mode
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractStore.similarity_search` defines default parent exclusion, but the existing implementations differ: PostgreSQL applies it explicitly, while Arango’s FTS and hybrid methods do not apply `metadata_filters` at all. Define the supported metadata filter grammar and apply it before vector, FTS, and hybrid limiting; test scalar, list, boolean, missing-key, and parent-marker cases.

suggestions.title: Prove the SDK async boundary before selecting the implementation
suggestions.rationale: The public store APIs are async, but the accepted design leaves the LanceDB async API and compatible release unresolved. A synchronous SDK call directly inside these methods would block the event loop; if no complete async API exists, isolate calls behind a bounded `asyncio.to_thread`/executor boundary and define connection ownership and shutdown behavior.

suggestions.title: Design and test true cross-process write behavior
suggestions.rationale: The settled requirement is concurrent writes from independent processes, which an asyncio lock cannot provide. Existing store write paths show upsert and batch behavior but no shared filesystem coordination; validate LanceDB’s guarantees for concurrent appends, colliding stable IDs, table creation, and index updates, adding an inter-process lock or documented conflict policy if needed.

suggestions.title: Make collection, FTS-index, and freshness lifecycle explicit
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractStore` exposes `create_collection` and `prepare_embedding_table`, while Arango creates views during connection and PostgreSQL prepares tables/indexes separately. LanceDB needs a specified startup path for table/schema validation, FTS-index creation, missing-index errors, visibility of newly written rows, and behavior while another process rebuilds an index.

suggestions.title: Define stable IDs independently of generated row keys
suggestions.rationale: `SearchResult.id` is required, but `Document` contains only `page_content` and metadata; existing backends generate UUIDs or use backend-specific keys. Specify ID precedence, persistence, duplicate/upsert behavior, and collection isolation so reopening a directory and concurrent writers cannot create duplicate logical documents.

suggestions.title: Complete optional-backend registration without eager imports
suggestions.rationale: Store selection is driven by the core `supported_stores` map and dynamic imports in `VectorInterface`; satellite tests currently assert the exact map and backend list. Add the LanceDB name/class mapping, optional extra, namespace import smoke test, and clear missing-extra error while preserving lazy SDK loading and existing backend defaults.

suggestions.title: Enforce whole-origin failure for hybrid errors
suggestions.rationale: `SearchOrigin` explicitly propagates adapter errors and `MultiStoreSearchToolkit` isolates failures per origin. The LanceDB origin should perform one native hybrid operation and raise on either failing leg, with no fallback or partial hits; the toolkit should then report that origin as errored while graph and other origins continue.

suggestions.title: Keep LanceDB federation outside GraphExpandedRetriever
suggestions.rationale: `GraphIndexOrigin` wraps `GraphExpandedRetriever`, whose seed path is explicitly based on `HybridPageIndexSearch` or `GraphIndexEmbedder`. Configure LanceDB as a sibling origin in the toolkit and test that it is not substituted into the graph retriever’s seed backend, matching the settled graph scope.

suggestions.title: Separate embedded storage from the fully-offline guarantee
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractStore` defaults to HuggingFace embeddings, while the workspace also supports Google and OpenAI providers through optional extras. A local LanceDB directory alone does not make the agent offline; define provisioning/runtime policy requiring a locally available embedding model and add a no-network acceptance test rather than claiming offline behavior from the backend.

suggestions.title: Build an acceptance matrix before performance claims
suggestions.rationale: The repository already tests origin normalization, per-origin failure isolation, native rank preservation, and exact store registration, but not persistence or backend semantics. Add a representative corpus and tests for restart, stable IDs, parent exclusion, metadata filters, vector/FTS/hybrid score provenance, missing/stale indexes, fresh-row visibility, hybrid-leg failure, fully offline execution, and multiprocessing writes before setting latency or recall targets.
